topics.title: Question Quest: Statistical Questions
topics.lesson:
**A statistical question expects answers that vary.**

- ✅ "How many pets do kids in my class have?" (lots of different answers)
- ❌ "How many pets do I have?" (one answer)

Tip: ask *many people* or measure *many times*!

examples.prompt: Is "How old are the students at Andrew's school?" statistical?

steps: "What were the test scores of my class?"
examples.answer: What were the test scores of the students in my class?

topics.title: Data Shapes: Center, Spread & Shape
topics.lesson:
**Every data set has a distribution.**

- **Center**: where the middle is (median, mean)
- **Spread**: how far apart values are (range, IQR)
- **Shape**: symmetric, skewed left/right, peaks, clusters, gaps

examples.prompt: Dot plot: 1: 1 dot; 2: 3 dots; 3: 5 dots; 4: 3 dots; 5: 1 dot. Shape?
Dot plot: 1: 5 dots; 2: 3 dots; 3: 1 dot; 6: 1 dot. Shape?

topics.title: Center Stage: Mean, Median, Mode & Range
topics.lesson:
**Measure of center = one number summary. Measure of variation = how spread out.**

- Mean: add all, divide by how many
- Median: middle value when in order (average the two middles if even)
- Mode: most frequent
- Range: max − min

topics.title: Picture Power: Dot Plots, Histograms & Box Plots
topics.lesson:
**Show data on a number line!**

- Dot plot: one dot per value
- Histogram: bars for ranges of values (intervals)
- Box plot: min, Q1, median, Q3, max
- Q1 = median of the lower half, Q3 = median of the upper half (leave out the middle number if the count is odd)

examples.prompt: IQR from box with Q1 = 3, Q3 = 9

topics.title: Data Detective: Summarizing & Choosing Measures
topics.lesson:
**Describe data like a pro.**

- Say how many observations and what was measured.
- MAD = average distance from the mean.
- IQR = Q3 − Q1.
- Outliers or skew? Use **median & IQR**. Symmetric? **Mean & MAD** work great.
